relations.subject: storage-engine:couchstore
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: minted - camelCase verb phrase; no existing predicate captures 'this axis is fixed by a choice made at resource-creation time, not a later mutable setting'. Directly answers this batch's hypothesis question about the storage-engine choice's temporal scope.
relations.evidence: You can choose between the Couchstore or Magma storage engines at the bucket level [when creating a bucket](manage-buckets.md#add-bucket).

relations.subject: storage-engine:magma
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: minted - same predicate as above, other value of the same choice
relations.evidence: You can choose between the Couchstore or Magma storage engines at the bucket level [when creating a bucket](manage-buckets.md#add-bucket). A single Capella cluster can have a mix of Couchstore and Magma buckets.

relations.subject: storage-engine:couchstore
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: minted - camelCase verb phrase; qualifies the chosenAtCreationTime finding - the choice is fixed at creation but not permanently immutable, since an explicit migration operation exists (either an API-driven swap rebalance on 7.6+/8.0, or a manual create-new-bucket-and-copy-data path on 7.2)
relations.evidence: Couchstore to Magma migration is only possible when the target Magma bucket has 1024 vBuckets. If your cluster in Capella uses Couchbase Server 7.6 or later, migrate your Couchstore buckets to Magma by making a [PUT - Migrate Buckets](../../management-api-reference/index.md#tag/Clusters/operation/putBucketStorageBackend) call to the Management API.

relations.subject: capella:management-api
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused (dependsOnService) - the storage-engine migration API operation depends on the Data Service being able to run a rebalance
relations.evidence: PUT - Migrate Buckets can migrate 1 or more Couchstore buckets to Magma while your cluster is running. The API runs a swap [rebalance](../scale-database.md#rebalance) of your cluster's Data Service nodes.

relations.subject: capella:xdcr
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused (availableSince) - object is an unconfirmed candidate id, see concept note; another instance of the known 'server-version-string citation on a Capella page' anomaly, recurring rather than new
relations.evidence: Only Couchbase Server 8.0 and later supports XDCR replication between buckets with different numbers of vBuckets. Couchstore buckets use 1024 vBuckets, while Magma buckets can use either 128 or 1024 vBuckets.

relations.subject: storage-engine:magma
relations.evidence: To copy the data, use [XDCR](../xdcr/xdcr.md) or [backup](../backup-restore.md) the Couchstore bucket and restore it to the new Magma bucket.

notable_absence.finding: No Enterprise/Community edition badge appears anywhere on this page - the storage-engine choice, and the migration path between engines, is presented as edition-agnostic (a Capella-tier/version distinction, not an Enterprise-vs-Community one). The known 'server-version-string citation' anomaly DOES recur here, three times over (7.6+, 7.2, and 8.0), which is unusually dense for a single Capella page - this is the batch's clearest example of that anomaly.

cross_component_finding: Directly answers this batch's hypothesis. (1) storage-engines.md confirms Couchstore/Magma cleanly as the only two storage engines - no third option is revealed, and the page is explicitly framed as binary ('Capella supports two different backend storage engines: Magma and Couchstore'). (2) The choice IS made at bucket-creation time ('at the bucket level when creating a bucket'), confirming the Health Advisor page's implicit framing - but the choice is not permanently fixed: an explicit, engine-specific migration path exists (PUT - Migrate Buckets API on 7.6+, or manual bucket-recreate-and-copy on 7.2), so 'creation-time choice' should be understood as 'default/initial choice, changeable only via a deliberate migration operation' rather than an immutable property. (3) A second, related but distinct axis is revealed: vBucket count (128 or 1024), which is itself a Magma-specific sub-choice with its own compatibility implications for XDCR - not previously visible from the single Health Advisor mention, and worth tracking separately from the storage-engine axis itself, though not promoted to its own concept here per the 'don't force it' rule (too thin a basis from one page). (4) The quantitative table (bucket memory quota, memory-to-data ratio, max data per node) gives Couchstore/Magma real comparative substance beyond the single resident-ratio threshold the Health Advisor page exposed, confirming this page as the authoritative source for the concept going forward.
cross_product_finding: capella:management-api's dependsOnService relation to service:data-service (via the storage-engine migration operation) is a new, concrete instance of a management-plane API call having a hard runtime dependency on a specific Couchbase service being deployed and healthy - consistent with, but more specific than, the service-dependency graph already established for Query/Index/Data/Analytics/Search Service pages.
